before_text: We propose a weakly supervised semantic segmentation method that utilizes large quantities and diversities in unlabeled videos to produce accurate, high-resolution results quickly. Our method utilizes motion cues found in video sequences to localize objects and classes. These cues are learned by an offline classifier, and their predictions are used as initial seed sets to propagate via graph cut optimization. Our method utilizes both spatial and temporal structural information, giving our system a good performance over static image-only learning frameworks as reported in literature. We also incorporate recent work, such as Deep Features (a Convolutional Neural Network), to improve overall accuracy and efficiency without significantly increasing run time cost. Our method significantly outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods such as PropNet and LTFS2K+N on public benchmark datasets such as Cityscapes, MPII, and CamVid, which are densely and significantly varied in their labeled regions.

before_text: Rogier Koordes, born on August 4, 1964, in Amsterdam, is a Dutch composer and musician. At the age of five, the piano played a significant role in his life. After playing classical music for a decade, he gradually switched to jazz in his late teens. In 1986, he was awarded a jazz piano scholarship by the Royal Dutch Conservatory in Amsterdam. Here, he started composing music and formed the Rogier Koordes Trio, with bassist Joris Roelofs and drummer Onno Muijs.  In 1990, he started collaborating and recording with several other musicians, including Dutch jazz musicians Benjamin Herman, Jesse van Ruller, and Cees Slinger, and American jazz musicians David Liebman, Joe Lovano, and Michael Brecker. He has performed with his own trio in Europe and once in New York. Since 1997, he has been a composer for Dutch National Television, creating music for numerous television programs. His musical Yellow Cold is commissioned by the Dutch Ballet and has been performed numerous times in The Netherlands since 2004.  In 2011, Koordes released the album "Songs for Fathers," for which he wrote lyrics for the first time in Dutch.
